title: RPG and adventure
summary: Experiences organized around exploration, character growth, authored or systemic challenges, and progress that gives players a reason to return.

designKnowledge.playerPromise: The player becomes more capable and learns more about a world by making choices and completing challenges.
coreLoop: make a tactical or social choice
use the consequence to unlock a new route or approach
designKnowledge.progression: Prefer layered short and long arcs. A reward should change available choices or player expression; numerical growth alone is not a complete progression loop.
designKnowledge.multiplayer: Decide which quest facts are personal, party-shared, or world-shared before building replication and reward rules.
designKnowledge.artAndAnimation: World landmarks, equipment silhouettes, enemy poses, and traversal animations must communicate goals and threat at Roblox camera distance.
productRisks: rewards that make early spaces irrelevant
quest state that diverges between party members
large worlds whose content density is not supported by production capacity

technicalPatterns.name: Separate quest definition from player quest state
technicalPatterns.guidance: Keep authored objectives and reward definitions in validated data; keep each player's authoritative completion state server-owned and versioned.

technicalPatterns.name: Stream content by player intent
technicalPatterns.guidance: For large worlds, establish a measured baseline device and test join, traversal, and encounter transitions before expanding the world footprint.

failureModes.description: Players cannot infer what progress requires or where it can happen.
failureModes.mitigation: Pair a concise objective with a visible world cue; test comprehension with a first-time player without verbal coaching.

failureModes.description: Party members receive inconsistent quest credit or rewards.
failureModes.mitigation: Define ownership and eligibility rules explicitly and run two-client tests for join, leave, retry, and duplicate completion.

scenarios.action: Give a new player a quest without verbal explanation.
scenarios.expected: The player can describe the goal, identify a next action, and recognize completion.

scenarios.action: Complete a shared objective with two clients, then test a late join and a rejoin.
scenarios.expected: Eligibility and rewards follow the declared party rules on the server.

acceptanceCriteria: Core progress is visible in the world and UI.
Quest credit is consistent for the declared single-player or party model.
The essential route remains legible at the certified mobile baseline.

considerations: Profile the densest traversal and encounter space on the certified baseline device.
Measure memory, draw work, and join time instead of setting universal part-count targets.

sourceRefs.title: Approved Lab game-family and hybrid scope

evidence.description: Structured family design record with a player loop, production roles, failure modes, and repeatable acceptance scenarios.

assumptions: This is a design knowledge package, not evidence that a complete RPG has been implemented or certified.
Subgenres are overlapping labels; a concept may combine several without becoming a template.
